- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or low; apply 1–2% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., 0.00 → 0.33 → 0.00), model often misreads momentum; adjust forecast to reflect slower decay or mean reversion.
- Forecasting from 30-day horizon shows persistent lag in price correction; add 1–2 days of delay in downward corrections (e.g., if true price drops 5%, forecast should drop 3–4%).
